title: King's English (1...e5)
intro: 1...e5 creates a Reversed Sicilian. Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, trade off ...d5, or expand on the queenside against ...Nc6.

lessons.title: Meeting 3...d5
lessons.summary: Trade on d5 and hit Black's knight with Bg2.

steps.text: Against 1...e5, White meets Black's central control with 2.Nc3 and 3.g3.
Play the King's English opening moves against 1...e5 and 2...Nf6.
steps.hint: c4, Nc3, then prepare Bg2 with g3.
steps.ifRight: The bishop is ready for g2.

steps.text: Black strikes in the centre at once with 3...d5.
Swap your flank pawn for Black's central d-pawn.
steps.hint: Capture on d5 with the c-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.cxd5 so you keep two central pawns to Black's one.
steps.ifRight: Black will recapture with the knight.

steps.text: Black takes back with 4...Nxd5.
Put your bishop on the long diagonal, hitting the knight on d5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Bg2 to pressure d5 and the queenside.
steps.ifRight: Now White develops Nf3, O-O and d3.

steps.text: Black retreats with 5...Nb6. Continue developing.
steps.hint: Develop the king's knight and attack e5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Nf3 to develop and pressure e5.
steps.ifRight: Next come O-O and d3, with a smooth position.

lessons.title: Meeting 2...Nc6
lessons.summary: Build a solid Botvinnik-style structure with g3, Bg2 and d3.

steps.text: Black often develops the queen's knight with 2...Nc6 to guard e5 and stop d4.
Prepare your kingside fianchetto.
steps.ifRight: White will put the bishop on g2.

steps.text: Black mirrors your plan with 3...g6.
Place your bishop on the long diagonal.
steps.hint: Move the f1 bishop to g2.
steps.ifRight: The bishop controls d5 and the long diagonal.

steps.text: Black completes the fianchetto with 4...Bg7.
Control e4 and open a diagonal for your dark-squared bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.d3 to stop ...e4 and support your dark squares.
steps.ifRight: White is ready for Nf3, O-O and Rb1.

steps.text: Black plays 5...d6. Choose a flexible developing move.
steps.hint: Develop the king's knight to f3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Nf3 (or 6.e4 or 6.Rb1) to prepare castling and queenside play.
steps.ifRight: Then O-O, Rb1 and b4 give White strong queenside play.

lessons.title: Meeting 3...Bb4
lessons.summary: Develop Bg2 and Nf3 calmly, and meet ...e4 with Nd4.

steps.text: Instead of 3...d5, Black can pin the c3 knight with 3...Bb4.
Keep developing and protect your queenside.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.Bg2: if Black takes on c3, bxc3 strengthens your centre.
steps.ifRight: The bishop sits safely on g2.

steps.text: Black castles: 4...O-O.
Develop your king's knight and attack e5.
steps.ifRight: White is ready to castle and play d4 or Nd5.

steps.text: Black pushes 5...e4 to chase your knight.
Jump forward to an active central square.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Nd4: the knight is well placed and e4 can be attacked later.
steps.ifRight: Next come O-O and d3 or Nc2, with a pleasant edge.
